subject: Deployability decision queue and variant costing — ops/product alignment
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Samantha Li <samantha.li@blackbirdhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Deployability decision queue and variant costing — ops/product alignment

Team —

Blackbird has formally asked for a path to run our inference runtime in their environment (US-only, PCI-scope for payments). They want an option that starts as a short pilot (4–8 weeks) with the ability to transition to a customer-managed on-prem variant later. They attached their MAP and the initial costing worksheet.

High-level asks from Blackbird:
- Pilot: isolated deployment (VPC-dedicated) or appliance in their colocation cage
- SLA target: 99.9% with 200ms p95 for standard chat workloads
- Audit needs: audit logs, KMS integration, and SOC2 evidence for data handling

Can infra/product/ops weigh in on feasibility + minimal staffing and timeline? I need a go/no-go recommendation and a recommended path (three options with rough staffing and cost delta) by EOD Monday so we can respond to Blackbird during next week's exec cadences.

Attachments: (blackbird-MAP.pdf, initial-variant-costing.xlsx)

Thanks —
Logan
Logan Wright
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Samantha Li <samantha.li@blackbirdhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Jul 2028 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployability decision queue and variant costing — ops/product alignment

Thanks Logan — quick first pass below. Quoting your note for context:
> Blackbird has formally asked for a path to run our inference runtime in their environment (US-only, PCI-scope for payments)...

Option A — Isolated VPC (hosted + network isolation):
- Description: Redwood-hosted, tenant-dedicated VPC with strict egress rules, dedicated GPU pool for the customer.
- Pros: Fastest to delivery (2–4 weeks for pilot), minimal changes to runtime.
- Cons: Requires network peering and cross-account IAM changes; still no full physical control for customer.
- Staffing: 0.5 PM, 1 SRE (pilot), 1 infra eng (network).
- Cost delta vs hosted: +35% unit cost.

Option B — Dedicated reserved capacity (customer-dedicated GPUs managed by Redwood):
- Description: Reserved GPU pool (isolation at compute level), customer data in separate storage accounts, integration for KMS.
- Pros: Aligns with our dedicated offering; clearer SLA guarantees.
- Cons: Longer lead time for capacity provisioning and procurement (4–6 weeks).
- Staffing: 1 PM, 1.5 SRE, 1 infra eng, 0.5 customer success for onboarding.
- Cost delta: +65% unit cost.

Option C — On-prem appliance (air-gapped or customer-managed HW):
- Description: Appliance image + runbook deployed in customer colocation. Requires on-prem ops onboarding, HSM/KMS integration via customer network, and a secure update channel.
- Pros: Meets strict control/compliance asks.
- Cons: Highest operational overhead, 8–12 week lead for pilot, requires oncall expansion and support SLAs negotiation.
- Staffing: 2 SREs for onboarding + 3x FTE EngOps to maintain pilot (first 3 months).
- Cost delta: bespoke pricing (T&M + unit premiums).

Architectural notes:
- KV cache and continuous batching will need to be validated in multi-tenant codepaths; recommend a compatibility smoke test during pilot.
- Quantized model variants are generally fine but will need local compilation testing for customer hardware if on-prem.
- SLA: we will need explicit exception for deterministic KV cache cold-starts in any pilot agreement.

I've attached a quick comparison sheet (arch-option-comparison.xlsx) with timelines and a first-pass resource table.

Next steps suggestion: pick an initial path (A or B recommended) to shorten delivery; treat C as a later-phase offering only if the customer requires physical control. I'll draft a runbook & resource plan if we greenlight pilot.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Architect, Serving Runtime
(attachment: arch-option-comparison.xlsx)
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Samantha Li <samantha.li@blackbirdhealth.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Jul 2028 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployability decision queue and variant costing — ops/product alignment

Appreciate the clear options Karthik — operational read below.

Operational constraints & asks:
- Pilot window: we can support a 6-week pilot for Option B (Dedicated reserved pool) but need procurement approval for committed instances or we will expose to capacity preemption.
- Oncall/runway: Option C triggers a material oncall expansion. For a pilot we estimate 2 SREs on rotation plus 1 eng for incident triage; long-term support would require hiring 2 more EngOps.
- Security/compliance: Blackbird's PCI scope means we must get IAM/KMS design signoff and an updated data retention policy. Naomi — can you take point on SOC2 evidence mapping and list missing artifacts?
- Procurement: finance needs a budget placeholder to secure GPUs if we go Option B. I will submit a formal request but need an estimate of committed vGPU counts (Karthik: please confirm 2x A100-equivalent for pilot?).

If Sales wants to move quickly, we should propose Option B pilot with a defined rollback (return-to-hosted) and an agreed carveout of responsibilities. Monica

Monica Patel
Director, Customer Operations
(attachment: pilot-runbook-draft.md)
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Samantha Li <samantha.li@blackbirdhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployability decision queue and variant costing — ops/product alignment

Summary / decision log:
Thanks all for the quick turn. Based on the tradeoffs we discussed, proposed path for Blackbird: begin with Option B (Dedicated reserved capacity) for a 6-week pilot, with a pre-agreed transition criteria to Option C only if Blackbird mandates physical colocation.

Action items (owners & due dates):
- Karthik: produce a 1.0 runbook (deploy + rollback + smoke tests) and a vGPU sizing confirmation (confirm A100-equivalent count) — due Aug 7.
- Monica: submit procurement request and placeholder budget for 2 committed GPUs; create the pilot onboarding checklist with Security items flagged — due Aug 4.
- Naomi: map SOC2 artifacts and list gaps for Blackbird review; collect current audit logs retention evidence — due Aug 3.
- Logan: prepare customer-facing pilot proposal and timeline; coordinate Sales to include the carveouts and service-level expectations — due Aug 5.

Links: pilot playbook draft and HubSpot record are attached in the thread (Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/blackbird/pilot-plan, HubSpot: HUB-4421).

If anything critical is missing, call it out now — otherwise I will send a concise SOW for Sales to share with Blackbird by EOD Wednesday.

Best —
Logan
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference
